businessModel: Open source (AGPL-3.0); BYO API keys or local models; monetisation not documented
updateCadence: Very frequent component releases on GitHub (server, extension, neo)
summary: AGPL-3.0 agentic Chromium fork for Mac, Windows and Linux. Run agents with your own API keys or local models (Ollama/LM Studio), or use neo as an agent-driven browser connected via MCP to Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.
bestFor: Developers who want agents controlling a real logged-in browser
Users wanting open-source AI browsing and BYO keys
notFor: People wanting a polished consumer assistant
Users expecting built-in sync or password manager

pros.title: Open source
pros.detail: AGPL-3.0 with a very active GitHub repo (about 14k stars).

pros.title: Bring your own model
pros.detail: Works with API keys or local models via Ollama and LM Studio.

pros.title: MCP integration
pros.detail: neo connects one-click to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and more.

pros.title: Linux support
pros.detail: AppImage and deb builds, rare among AI browsers.

pros.title: Privacy transparency
pros.detail: Neo keeps sessions locally and says it never sends URLs, prompts or screenshots; telemetry has one off toggle.

cons.title: Local models are weak for agents
cons.detail: Docs warn local models are not yet strong enough for Agent Mode.

cons.title: No sync or password manager documented
cons.detail: Only one-time Chrome import is mentioned.

cons.title: Rapid, fragmented releases
cons.detail: Component-based tags make versions hard to track; AGPL may deter some.

jsSpeed: Blink/V8 engine, Chrome-class JS speed; no vendor benchmark
pageLoad: Chromium rendering; AI sidebar adds overhead
networkSpeed: Chromium network stack with HTTP/3 and preloading
startup: Chromium cold start, heavier than plain Chrome
memory: Chromium multi-process plus AI layer; RAM-heavy
cpu: Chromium-class; agent tasks add background load
lowEnd: Chromium plus local models need strong hardware
installSize: Full Chromium bundle, a few hundred MB
privacyDefaults: Local data, ungoogled patches, BYO keys
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox; agent injection risk remains
patchSpeed: Small team tracking Chromium; lag unmeasured
telemetry: Anonymous events, single opt-out, no URLs sent
behaviourCustom: Few shortcut or per-site options documented
advancedSettings: Chromium flags, MCP and key settings
tabManagement: Tab groups and search; no workspaces documented
searchFreedom: Default search changeable; AI prompt flow is the focus
productivity: AI sidebar, page chat and summaries
translation: AI-driven page translation; no dedicated engine
accessibility: Chromium accessibility stack, unverified for AI layer
businessTrust: Open code, transparent telemetry, small company
ai: Agent Mode, MCP and local model support
beginnerFriendly: Needs API keys or local setup for AI
